stem: Meera stirs a spoonful of sugar into a glass of water until no sugar grains can be seen, yet the water still tastes sweet. Which statement best explains what has happened to the sugar?

options.text: The sugar particles have disappeared, and only the sweetness is left in the water.
The sugar particles have separated and spread into the spaces between the water particles, so sugar is present throughout the water.
The sugar has melted into liquid sugar, which sits at the bottom of the glass.
Each sugar particle has gone inside a water particle, making the water particles sweet.

teacher.key_rationale: Dissolving is a physical process in which sugar particles separate and occupy the spaces between water particles; the sugar is still present throughout the solution, which is why it tastes sweet even though no grains are visible. A, C and D reflect common wrong ideas (sugar vanishing, melting, or entering water particles).
